latest.title: ATM Facility Update, Second Block Admission & TVR
latest.content:
15 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 7170U
Caledonian Holdings PLC
15 September 2026
This announcement contains inside information for the purposes of Article 7 of the UK version of Regulation (EU) No 596/2014, as it forms part of UK domestic law by virtue of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018, as amended ("MAR"). Upon the publication of this announcement, this inside information is now considered to be in the public domain.
15 September 2026
Caledonian Holdings PLC
("Caledonian" or the "Company")
ATM Facility Update, Second Block Admission and Total Voting Rights
Caledonian Holdings PLC (AIM: CHP), the AIM quoted investing company focused on building an integrated financial services group, provides an update on the At the Market Facility (the "ATM Facility") established with Axis Capital Markets Limited ("Axis"), as announced on 19 June 2026. To date, the Company has raised gross proceeds of approximately £644,147 pursuant to the ATM Facility through the issue of a total of 41,303,724 new ordinary shares (the "ATM Shares") at an average price of 1.55954 pence per ATM Share. The Company also confirms that the 26,010,702 Ordinary Shares pursuant to the initial block admission as announced on 1 July 2026 (the "First Block Listing Shares") have now been fully allotted.
No further shares will be allotted under this block admission, which is expected to be cancelled on 18 September 2026. A further application will be made for the admission of 15,293,022 new Ordinary Shares pursuant to the ATM Facility to trading on AIM ("ATM Facility Admission"). ATM Facility Admission is expected to become effective and dealings to commence at 8.00 a.m. on or around 18 September 2026.
The net proceeds from the ATM Facility will be used to repay part of the funding provided by Yorkville Advisors Global, LP as announced on 14 November 2025, and for general working capital purposes.
The Company also announces that it intends to apply to the London Stock Exchange for a second block admission in respect of up to 44,063,447 new Ordinary Shares of nominal value £0.01 each in the Company to trading on AIM ("Second Block Listing Shares"), representing approximately 20% of the Company's enlarged issued share capital, following the allotment of all the First Block Listing Shares and the ATM Facility Admission. The Second Block Listing Shares will be issued to Axis or its appointed custodian pursuant to the ATM Facility (the "Second ATM Tranche"), and Axis will use reasonable endeavours to sell the Second ATM Tranche during the remaining term of the ATM Facility (the minimum term of which is one year, as announced on 19 June 2026), subject to the customary selling restrictions set out in that announcement. The Second ATM Tranche will be issued fully paid and will rank
pari passu
in all respects with the Company's existing Ordinary Shares. The Company intends to provide periodic updates on the proceeds of the sale of the Second ATM Tranche.
Application will be made to the London Stock Exchange for the admission of the Second Block Listing Shares to trading on AIM ("Second Block Listing Admission"). Second Block Listing Admission is expected to become effective and dealings to commence at 8.00 a.m. on or around 21 September 2026. The Second Block Listing Shares will be in place for an initial six month period from Admission.
Total Voting Rights
Following the allotment of all the First Block Listing Shares and the ATM Facility Admission, the Company's issued share capital will comprise 220,317,235 ordinary shares of £0.01 each ("Ordinary Shares") with one voting right each. The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in treasury. Therefore, the total number of Ordinary Shares and voting rights in the Company is 220,317,235.
The above figure may be used by shareholders in the Company as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, the share capital of the Company under the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.

latest.title: Launch of Aspire Business Account and Debit Card
latest.content:
9 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 9223T
Caledonian Holdings PLC
09 September 2026
9 September 2026
Caledonian Holdings PLC
("Caledonian" or the "Company")
COMMERCIAL LAUNCH OF ASPIRE MULTI-CURRENCY BUSINESS CURRENT ACCOUNT AND MASTERCARD DEBIT CARD
Caledonian Holdings PLC (AIM: CHP),
the AIM quoted investing company focused on building an integrated financial services group, is pleased to announce that Aspire Commerce Group Limited ("Aspire"), its wholly owned subsidiary, has completed the commercial launch of its enhanced multi-currency business current account proposition, including the Mastercard World Business Debit Card.
The launch represents a key commercial milestone identified in the Company's £612,000 fundraising announced on 13 August 2026, which was undertaken in part to accelerate Aspire's business account and debit card rollout and progress its trade finance pipeline. With the enhanced proposition now commercially available, Aspire's focus will move to growing its customer base through direct and partnership-led distribution, increasing transaction volumes and converting its existing trade finance opportunities into recurring revenues.
Highlights
·
Mastercard World Business Debit Card now integrated with Aspire's multi-currency business account proposition.
·
One platform brings together multi-currency account functionality, domestic and international payments, foreign exchange and debit card capability.
·
The account supports business payments including faster payments, direct debits, standing orders, payroll and international supplier payments.
·
Eligible business customers can apply for trade finance directly alongside their day-to-day account activity, with facilities of up to £5 million for periods of up to 120 days.
·
The expanded proposition increases Aspire's opportunity to generate recurring account, transaction and foreign-exchange revenues, while supporting the expansion and scaling of its trade finance activities.
·
Aspire combines in-house, wholly owned digital infrastructure with UK-based relationship support for businesses undertaking domestic and international trade.
·
Aspire's go-to-market strategy combines direct customer acquisition with partner-led and white-label distribution, providing multiple routes to scale customer numbers and revenues without requiring a corresponding increase in direct customer acquisition expenditure.
Integrated business finance proposition
Muloot Money is the trading name of Aspire's international multi-currency financial services platform for business customers. The enhanced proposition is designed to reduce the need for internationally trading businesses to use multiple providers for their everyday account, payments, foreign exchange, card and working-capital requirements, by bringing these services together through an integrated platform.
Businesses can hold and manage multiple currencies, send and receive domestic and international payments, manage foreign exchange and use the Mastercard debit card for day-to-day expenditure. For eligible customers, trade finance can be accessed alongside the account, enabling funding for import and export transactions to be linked more closely with daily cash-flow management.
The platform is also capable of supporting white-label deployments, either for individual services such as onboarding, cards and foreign exchange, or as a broader account and trade finance proposition, providing Aspire with additional routes to market.
Strategic significance for Caledonian
Caledonian acquired Aspire on 1 June 2026 as the cornerstone operating business within its strategy to build an integrated financial services group. The commercial launch of the enhanced business current account proposition is an important step in expanding Aspire's support to SME's via its proprietary fintech solutions.
Jim McColl, Executive Director of Caledonian Holdings plc, commented:
"This is exactly the type of commercial milestone we said the August 2026 fundraising would unlock. Aspire now has a commercially available proposition bringing together a multi-currency business account, international payments, foreign exchange, a Mastercard debit card and access to trade finance through one wholly owned platform.
Importantly, this is not a platform development announcement; the infrastructure is built, the debit card is live and the focus now moves to growing the customer base, increasing transaction volumes and accelerating the trade finance pipeline into revenue.
We believe the combination of day-to-day business financial services with integrated access to trade finance is a genuine differentiator for Aspire and an important step in building a revenue-generating operating business within Caledonian that has the ability to scale via organic customer acquisition and a partnership program that is driven by superior infrastructure."
Adam Rigler, Chief Executive Officer of Aspire, commented:
"Internationally trading businesses are often forced to use separate providers for accounts, payments, foreign exchange, cards and working capital. Muloot Money has been designed to bring those services together in one environment, supported by a UK-based team that understands the needs of growing businesses.
The launch of the Mastercard debit card completes an important part of that proposition. Our attention now is on commercial rollout, customer acquisition and helping more businesses use the platform to manage and finance their trade."
Regulatory information
Muloot Money is a trading name of Aspire Payments Limited. Aspire Payments Limited is registered with the Financial Conduct Authority as a Small Electronic Money Institution to issue electronic money and provide payment services under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011 (FRN 900883). The Muloot Money Mastercard World Business Debit Card is issued by Transact Payments Limited pursuant to a licence from Mastercard International Incorporated.

company_30s.what_they_do: CHP is a UK‑based financial services group that specialises in providing banking‑as‑a‑service solutions and fintech products, including a new Aspire Business Account and debit card aimed at small‑to‑mid‑size firms.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company sits at the intersection of traditional banking and modern digital payments, a sector that is rapidly expanding as businesses seek cheaper, faster, and more flexible financial tools. CHP’s platform offers a scalable, cloud‑native infrastructure that can be licensed to other banks and fintechs, giving it a potential moat in a market that is still consolidating.
company_30s.current_state: CHP is currently in a restructuring phase, raising fresh capital to fund its Aspire rollout while tightening its balance sheet. The stock is trading at a fraction of its historical highs, reflecting a steep pullback that many view as a capitulation point.

rns_narrative: The company has been actively reshaping its capital structure – a resignation of a director, a new ATM facility, and the admission of fundraising shares all point to a focus on liquidity and governance.
At the same time, CHP has launched the Aspire Business Account, signalling a pivot toward a product‑led growth model that could unlock new revenue streams and broaden its customer base.
Collectively, these moves suggest the firm is stabilising its operations while positioning itself for a future where it can monetize its technology platform.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Bullish optimism around a fintech pivot
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls are excited about the Aspire launch and the fresh capital, arguing that the platform could become a key player in the SME payments space.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the recent dilution and leadership shake‑up could erode shareholder value, and that regulatory hurdles might delay the bank licence that underpins the company’s long‑term strategy.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The community is quiet now, but the tone is gradually leaning bullish as more posts celebrate the new product and funding announcements.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat – no search interest. That silence is a good sign for a contrarian play because it means the market has not yet priced in any upside.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the current fundraising round and a clear timeline for the bank licence approval could act as a trigger for a sharp bounce.
A spike in trading volume around the launch of the Aspire debit card would signal renewed interest from both retail and institutional investors.
Price touching the 50‑day moving average and breaking above the recent low would provide a technical confirmation that the bottom is solid.
expect_next.watch_for: Key data points: (1) Any announcement of a new funding tranche or a bank licence, (2) a sustained volume increase of at least 30% above the 30‑day average, (3) price action that closes above the 50‑day MA and remains above the support level for three consecutive sessions.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is deep in a 70‑95% crash, the APEX score indicates a tight compression, and the recent RNS activity shows that the company is still in a recovery phase. A mean‑reversion bounce is expected once the market confirms the new product and capital structure.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The signal colour is GREEN, which historically delivers a 39% average return with a 40% win rate. If the price recovers to the mid‑range of its 52‑week high, the upside is roughly 200% from the current level. The deep crash and lack of public sentiment create a high‑reward, low‑probability scenario that aligns with the contrarian strategy.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The risk is that the dilution from new shares could push the share price lower, and regulatory delays could stall the bank licence. In the worst case, the stock could stay below the current low for an extended period, eroding investor confidence.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is capped at the current price (the worst you can lose is 100% of your capital if the stock stays flat or declines further). Potential gain, if the price moves to the mid‑range, is about 200%. The asymmetry is roughly 1:2, favouring upside.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above the 50‑day MA if volume spikes >30% above the 30‑day average. Size the position so that the stop, set 10% below entry, limits loss to less than 5% of the portfolio.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until the next RNS confirms a bank licence or a new funding round. Watch for a 20% volume jump on the launch day of the Aspire debit card; that would be a clear signal to enter.
playbook.if_passing: No immediate terminal risks, so no need to pass. The only real risk would be a sudden regulatory denial or a catastrophic dilution event.

ai_insights.bottom_line: CHP is a deep‑crashed fintech that has just launched a promising product and raised fresh capital – a classic contrarian set‑up with a high upside and a very limited downside.
